private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery and automatic distribution, reflecting the identifiable class and the value of avoiding certification and trial risk. Request fees in addition to the class fund, with court review preserved and any amount not awarded benefiting the class rather than Brightline.

The case has meaningful merits value, but certification risk and delay support pursuing a substantial certain recovery. Automatic payments are important because Brightline can identify every member. I will open with a high class fund and seek fee terms that protect the class if the court awards less than requested.

Keep total outlay well below the $40 million ceiling while making automatic distribution a strong, credible term given Brightline’s complete records. Open with the same complete counteroffer to both firms; reserve room to negotiate. Do not accept either current proposal, both of which exceed the authorized cap.

The $25 million automatic fund is a meaningful offer, but it is below the class's risk-adjusted litigation value even before accounting for the competing actions and the value of prompt, certain recovery. Counter at $32 million for the class, keep fees separate and subject to court approval, and preserve automatic distribution. Reject fee reversion so any amount the court declines to award benefits the class. Do not accept the current offer yet.

The defense’s automatic-payment term is valuable and should be preserved. The class fund is the priority; fees do not affect counsel’s compensation, and any fee the court declines should benefit the class rather than Brightline. Make a meaningful but not final concession from the opening demand while maintaining a substantial class recovery.

Hargrove Lane’s latest proposal totals $37 million, within the $40 million authorization, and provides automatic payments with no clear-sailing commitment. Accepting it secures a lower-outlay settlement and releases the overlapping claims. Do not disclose the separate negotiations to Whitcombe Reyes.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties reached the settlement through arms-length negotiations. The agreed terms provide a $32,000,000 class fund and $5,000,000 in attorneys’ fees and expenses, with fees paid separately from the class fund and subject to court approval. Brightline did not agree to clear sailing, and any fees not awarded will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. Payments will be made automatically to identified class members. Consistent with the confidentiality of the mediation communications, this statement does not recount the parties’ offers or counteroffers.
